steps.name: Hallmark GSEA on treated vs control DE ranks
caveats: Only 12000 genes are present in the input versus ~20000 in the full human genome/reference used to build hallmark sets, so some hallmark gene set members will not be present in the ranked list — report the fraction of matched genes per hallmark set to flag any set with poor coverage

Sample sample_01 (library size ~4x below median) already affected the upstream DESeq2 fit that produced de_results.csv; this cannot be corrected retroactively at the enrichment step and should be noted as a caveat carried into the interpretation of results
With only 12 samples total (6 vs 6) the DE ranking may be statistically underpowered for weak-effect genes, which can attenuate GSEA significance for pathways with modest but consistent shifts
steps.context: Input is a 12000-gene DESeq2 results table (gene, base_mean, log2_fold_change, log2fc SE/stat, p-value, padj) for the treated (AD lesional) vs control (6 vs 6, unpaired) contrast in human skin. This table is a finished DE analysis, not raw counts, so this step only needs to rank genes and run enrichment — no normalization, batch correction, or count modeling is needed. The human MSigDB Hallmark gene sets (50 sets, HGNC symbols) are staged in the reference store as a GMT file; resolve its current path via the reference lookup available in the sandbox rather than hardcoding a path from this plan, since the store layout is an installer detail.
steps.question: Which of the 50 MSigDB Hallmark pathways are significantly enriched (up or down) in the AD lesional (treated) versus control skin DESeq2 contrast, based on the existing de_results.csv (12000 genes)?
constraints: Use Python only, per user constraint — do not use R/fgsea even though it is installed
Do not re-run DESeq2 or otherwise regenerate differential expression; the provided de_results.csv is the sole source of gene-level statistics
Match gene identifiers by HGNC symbol (both the DE table and the Hallmark GMT are gene-symbol keyed) — do not attempt ID conversion via UniProt mapping, it is unnecessary here
Resolve the Hallmark GMT reference path at execution time rather than assuming the path shown in planning-time context is still current
acceptance_criteria: Reads /eval-full-32-without-python-enrichment-only-2/data/inputs/results/de_results.csv and builds a ranked gene list using a signed statistic (prefer DESeq2 'stat' column if present, else sign(log2_fold_change)*-log10(p-value)), dropping genes with missing/NA values and de-duplicating gene symbols by keeping the entry with the largest |rank metric|
Runs gseapy.prerank (or equivalent pre-ranked GSEA) against the 50-term MSigDB human Hallmark gene set (HALLMARK_* names) resolved from the reference store at run time, using >=1000 permutations
Output table lists all 50 hallmark terms with NES, p-value, FDR q-value, gene set size, and leading-edge gene list, sorted by FDR
Reports pathways significant at FDR < 0.05 explicitly, separated by direction of NES (up in treated vs down in treated)
Saves a bar/dot plot of top significant hallmark terms ranked by NES with FDR annotated
Script explicitly checks for the hallmark GMT file's presence before running and fails clearly (not silently) if absent

plan.title: Hallmark pathway enrichment: AD lesional vs control skin
plan.analytical_narrative: The DE results table (12000 genes x 8 columns, DESeq2 treated vs control contrast, gene/base_mean/log2_fold_change/etc.) already exists as an analysis input, so no re-computation of differential expression is needed. The research question asks specifically which MSigDB Hallmark pathways are enriched between the treated (AD lesional) and control groups. The plan runs a single Python-based pre-ranked GSEA (gseapy.prerank, using the DESeq2 stat or a signed -log10(p)*sign(log2FC) rank metric) against the 50 human MSigDB Hallmark gene sets staged in the reference store, then reports significant pathways (FDR < 0.05) with normalized enrichment scores and leading-edge genes. A single enrichment-agent step suffices because the input is already a ranked gene list (gene-level DE table), not a raw count matrix requiring further processing.
